newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields dip on back of crown, EMU.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields dip on back of crown, EMU.

text.p: Swedish bond yields were trading lower in fairly quiet trade at midday Wednesday, spurred by a firmer crown and cautious optimism on Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
"The market is thrown between hope and despair and will probably continue to be so during the coming days with all these meetings in Europe," an analyst said.
There was also interest on Sweden's first quarter GDP-figure, due to be published at 1100 GMT.
A Reuters poll found the market was expecting a 1.6 percent rise.
Ten-year bond yields dropped three basis points to 6.93 percent while the six-month T-bill rate dipped one basis point to 4.19 percent.
The crown was firmer against both the dollar and the mark with no major movements expected during the rest of the day.
The mark softened to 4.5285 crowns compared to 4.5380 crowns late Tuesday.
Dealers said the market's main focus now was the European Union heads of state and government summit in Amsterdam on June 16/17.
